questions.stem: Regarding Raster and vector: a designer reviewing a farmer's market sign notices that a pixel-based logo becomes blurry when it is scaled up. Which representation would stay sharp at any size?

options.text: A higher-resolution raster copy of the very same logo
options.misconception: treats more pixels as equivalent to true resolution independence

options.text: A vector graphic defined by mathematical paths
A raster image saved under a different file extension
options.misconception: confuses the file format name with the underlying structure

options.text: A photograph of the logo captured at a much larger size
options.misconception: mistakes capture size for genuine scalability

questions.explanation: Raster images are grids of pixels and lose clarity when enlarged beyond their resolution. Vector graphics store shapes as mathematical paths, so they scale without blurring, which is why logos are usually built as vectors.
questions.hint: Which representation does not depend on a fixed grid of pixels?
